narrativeReportMd:
# ContactPoint R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
No hard local instance-breaking changes were found for `ContactPoint`. The ContactPoint element set, cardinalities, primitive/datatype choices, required binding strengths, modifier flags, summary flags, and core validation invariant are stable between R4 and the R6 ballot build.

## Scope
This assessment covers the ContactPoint datatype itself and its directly bound ContactPoint terminology. Base-artifact changes, especially the R6 move of datatypes under `DataType` rather than directly under `Element`, are out of scope for ContactPoint findings and should be handled by the DataType/base reports.

## Main migration themes
The main local migration concern is semantic rather than structural: R6 expands the `ContactPoint.rank` comment to explicitly allow duplicate ranks, non-sequential ranks, and unranked repetitions. Implementations that used stricter local ordering assumptions should review contact-selection and sorting logic.

The required bindings for `system` and `use` point to R6-versioned ValueSets, but the local complete CodeSystems contain the same code lists as R4. This is a terminology package/version update, not a code-removal break.

## Highest-impact findings
No Critical or High local findings were identified. The only local finding is Low impact and concerns runtime interpretation of `rank`.

## Findings requiring human review
No finding requires human review based on the supplied local computable definitions. Reviewers may still want the official R4-to-R6 diff or ballot change notes to confirm whether the `rank` text was intended as a pure clarification.

## Backward-compatible design observations
The observed local changes are mostly additive metadata or clarifying text. R6 preserved the wire shape of ContactPoint, avoiding instance-level migration transforms.

## Follow-up analysis
Analyze the `DataType` and `Element` base artifacts separately for the class-hierarchy and inherited constraint metadata changes.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: No hard local ContactPoint breaking changes were found. The main migration concern is the R6 clarification that `rank` values need not be unique or sequential; terminology bindings are version-updated but retain the same required codes. The main uncertainty is absence of an official diff or change note explaining whether the rank wording is purely clarifying.
summary.migrationThemesMd: R4 ContactPoint instances should generally validate structurally as R6 ContactPoint instances if base-artifact changes are handled elsewhere. Migration work should focus on updating generated R6 model/terminology packages, verifying contact-ranking business logic, and ensuring validators use the R6 versions of the required ContactPoint ValueSets.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for computable structure, cardinality, type, flag, invariant, and local terminology conclusions because both StructureDefinitions and complete local CodeSystems were compared. Confidence is slightly lower for the intent of narrative/comment changes because no official diff, Jira issue, or full rendered narrative comparison was available.

findings.title: R6 clarifies that ContactPoint.rank values need not be unique or sequential

oldState.summary: Rank was an optional positiveInt with only a brief comment that rank does not necessarily follow instance order.

semanticText.short: Specify preferred order of use (1 = highest)
semanticText.definition: Specifies a preferred order in which to use a set of contacts. ContactPoints with lower rank values are more preferred than those with higher rank values.
semanticText.comment: Note that rank does not necessarily follow the order in which the contacts are represented in the instance.

oldState.narrativeMd: In R4, `rank` was structurally optional and had no invariant requiring uniqueness, sequential numbering, or presence on all repetitions. The comment only warned that rank is independent of array order.

newState.summary: Rank remains an optional positiveInt, but the comment now explicitly allows duplicate ranks, non-sequential ranks, and repetitions without rank.

semanticText.short: Specify preferred order of use (1 = highest)
semanticText.definition: Specifies a preferred order in which to use a set of contacts. ContactPoints with lower rank values are more preferred than those with higher rank values.
semanticText.comment:
Note that rank does not necessarily follow the order in which the contacts are represented in the instance.

Ranks need not be unique.  E.g. it's possible to have multiple contacts with rank=1.  If the ranks have different systems or uses, this would be interpreted to mean "X is my most preferred phone number, Y is my most preferred email address" or "X is my preferred home email and Y is my preferred work email".  If the system and use for equally-ranked contacts are the same, then the level of preference is equivalent for both repetitions. 

Ranks need not be sequential and not all repetitions must have a rank.  For example, it's possible to have 4 contacts with ranks of 2, 5 and two with no rank specified.  That would be interpreted to mean the first is preferred over the second and no preference stated for the remaining contacts.

newState.narrativeMd: In R6, the wire-format and validation rules for `rank` remain the same, but the comment gives explicit semantic guidance for equal ranks, gaps, and omitted ranks.

facts.oldValue: Note that rank does not necessarily follow the order in which the contacts are represented in the instance.
facts.newValue: Adds explicit guidance that ranks need not be unique, need not be sequential, and need not appear on all repetitions.
facts.note: No cardinality, type, invariant, modifier flag, or summary flag changed for `ContactPoint.rank`.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is not a hard validation break: an R4 instance with duplicate, sparse, or missing ranks was not prohibited by the R4 cardinality, type, or constraints, and the R6 datatype still uses optional `positiveInt`. The practical risk is runtime interpretation. Systems that imposed local assumptions such as unique ranks, sequential ranks, or sorting unranked contacts after all ranked contacts may need to align with the R6 clarification.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Contact ranking can affect which phone number, email, or other contact point is tried first. Misinterpreting equal or missing ranks could cause suboptimal contact routing, but no direct clinical safety break is evident from the datatype definition alone.

justification.inferredGoal: Clarify how to interpret existing rank values without changing the ContactPoint wire format.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No less-breaking base-design alternative is needed because R6 preserved the ContactPoint wire shape and validation constraints; it only clarified rank interpretation in text.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred R6 goal is to clarify ambiguous `ContactPoint.rank` interpretation. That goal is reasonable, and using the element comment is probably justified because R6 keeps `rank` optional, keeps the `positiveInt` type, adds no uniqueness or sequencing invariant, and does not make R4-valid ContactPoint instances invalid. The remaining uncertainty is only that no official change note was available to confirm intent.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Under the calibration rules, the old external-guidance option is not a backward-compatible base R6 design alternative; it is a documentation placement choice. The base design is already backward-compatible for R4-to-R6 instances because duplicate, sparse, or absent ranks were not forbidden by the R4 StructureDefinition and remain structurally representable in R6.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Publishing the same guidance outside the StructureDefinition would be less visible and would not preserve additional R4 instances because none are invalidated by the R6 change.

evidence.detail: R4 only states that rank does not necessarily follow the order in which contacts are represented in the instance.
evidence.quote: Note that rank does not necessarily follow the order in which the contacts are represented in the instance.

evidence.detail: R6 adds guidance that ranks need not be unique, need not be sequential, and need not be present on every repetition.
evidence.quote: Ranks need not be unique. ... Ranks need not be sequential and not all repetitions must have a rank.

evidence.detail: R4 has cardinality 0..1, type positiveInt, isSummary true, and no local invariant on rank uniqueness or sequence.
R6 keeps cardinality 0..1, type positiveInt, isSummary true, and no local invariant on rank uniqueness or sequence.

examples.examplesMd: The example is an illustrative list of ContactPoint fragments, not a complete resource. It shows patterns R6 explicitly describes: equal ranks across different systems, a gap in rank numbering, and an unranked contact.

findings.narrativeMd: `ContactPoint.rank` did not change structurally, but R6 makes its semantics more explicit. Implementers should not assume that rank values are globally unique, contiguous, or present on every contact point. The likely migration issue is not validator rejection; it is application logic that sorts, de-duplicates, or selects contact points using stricter assumptions than the R6 comment supports.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-valid ContactPoint data is not made invalid by this change because the cardinality, `positiveInt` type, and constraints are unchanged. R6-valid ContactPoint data with equal ranks or rank gaps is syntactically representable in R4. The compatibility risk is behavioral: older R4 consumers or generated helper methods might impose local rank rules that were never encoded in the R4 StructureDefinition.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Review code that orders or selects telecom/contact arrays by `rank`. Tests should cover duplicate rank values, gaps such as ranks 2 and 5, and missing rank values. If local profiles require unique or sequential ranks for business reasons, keep those rules profile-specific rather than treating them as base ContactPoint requirements.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Because the change is a text clarification with no wire-format or validation tightening, it is largely backward-compatible. A fully non-disruptive alternative would have been external guidance only, but embedding the clarification in the StructureDefinition comment improves consistency for generated documentation and implementer tooling.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: If an official ballot change note shows this was intended to impose new conformance semantics rather than clarify existing freedom, impact may need to be raised for implementations that validate business rules around rank uniqueness.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: Canonical URL, id, name, kind, type, derivation, abstract flag, and active status are stable. The baseDefinition change from `Element` to `DataType` is acknowledged but treated as an inherited datatype-hierarchy issue outside this ContactPoint report.

The snapshot element ids are the same: `ContactPoint`, `ContactPoint.id`, `ContactPoint.extension`, `ContactPoint.system`, `ContactPoint.value`, `ContactPoint.use`, `ContactPoint.rank`, and `ContactPoint.period`.
All ContactPoint-local child elements keep the same cardinalities: `system`, `value`, `use`, `rank`, and `period` remain `0..1`; the datatype root remains `0..*`.
`system` and `use` remain `code`, `value` remains `string`, `rank` remains `positiveInt`, and `period` remains `Period`. There are no ContactPoint choice-type additions or removals.
ContactPoint has no reference-typed local elements in either R4 or R6.

`system` and `use` both retain required bindings to the same canonical ValueSets, updated from `|4.0.1` to `|6.0.0-ballot4`. The local complete CodeSystems have no added or removed codes; `ContactPointSystem.sms` has only a wording change from "an sms" to "a sms".

The local ContactPoint invariant `cpt-2` remains an error with expression `value.empty() or system.exists()`, so a value still requires a system. R6 adds condition metadata linking `ContactPoint.value` to `cpt-2`, but the validation expression itself is unchanged.
No fixed value, pattern, or defaultValue constraints were found on ContactPoint-local elements in either version.
No local maxLength, regex, minValue, or maxValue changes were identified for ContactPoint elements.
`ContactPoint.use` remains the only local modifier element, with the same modifier reason about not mistaking temporary or old contacts for current/permanent ones.
`system`, `value`, `use`, `rank`, and `period` remain summary elements. `id` and `extension` remain non-summary inherited elements.
ContactPoint defines no local slicing. The open slicing on `extension` is inherited/base behavior and was not treated as a local ContactPoint issue.

No local ContactPoint element was added, removed, renamed, moved, or retyped, so the JSON/XML wire shape for ContactPoint-specific content is stable. Base-class serialization concerns are delegated to the DataType/Element analyses.

For ContactPoint-local content, R6 adds no new element, code, type, or required value that R4 cannot carry. R6 content remains structurally representable in R4, subject to out-of-scope base-artifact differences.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Required binding ValueSet versions updated to R6 ballot versions without code-list changes
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: `ContactPoint.system` and `ContactPoint.use` remain required bindings to the same canonical ValueSet URLs. The local complete CodeSystems contain the same codes in R4 and R6: `phone`, `fax`, `email`, `pager`, `url`, `sms`, `other` for system, and `home`, `work`, `temp`, `old`, `mobile` for use. No R4-valid code is removed.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Terminology validators and generated enum packages should be updated to the R6 package/version. Systems that compare versioned ValueSet canonical strings should expect `|6.0.0-ballot4` instead of `|4.0.1`.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 links ContactPoint.value to the existing cpt-2 condition metadata
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The actual invariant remains `value.empty() or system.exists()` with severity `error`. Adding `condition: ["cpt-2"]` to `ContactPoint.value` improves computable traceability but does not create a new validation rule.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Generated documentation, validator diagnostics, or model metadata may now show `value` as directly affected by `cpt-2`. Instance migration is not required.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Publisher/contact/jurisdiction and standards-status metadata refreshed
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R6 package and resource metadata reflect the ballot build and FHIR Infrastructure work group, but ContactPoint's canonical identity and active normative status are preserved.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Metadata-sensitive tooling should tolerate package-version and publisher/contact changes when resolving the same ContactPoint canonical URL.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: R6 ContactPoint derives from `DataType` rather than directly from `Element`. This may affect generated class hierarchies and inherited metadata, but the assignment requires such base-artifact changes to be handled by the DataType/base reports rather than as local ContactPoint findings.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No official R4-to-R6 ContactPoint diff, Jira ticket, or ballot change note was available in the local inputs. The report infers change intent from computable definitions.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: An official HL7 change note or rendered diff explaining the `rank` comment expansion would confirm whether it is intended as a clarification or a normative semantic change.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: Terminology comparison used local complete CodeSystems and ValueSet compose definitions, not a live terminology-server expansion.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: A terminology expansion against both package versions would independently confirm that no codes were added, removed, or redefined in the required bindings.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The assessment did not analyze every resource or profile that embeds ContactPoint. Such artifacts may add their own ContactPoint cardinality, slicing, or rank rules.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Cross-artifact profile/resource analyses would identify additional implementation-guide-specific breaks, but those would not be local changes to the base ContactPoint datatype.
